writeup.headline: DocuSign rates Buy on a net-cash balance sheet, strong cash margins and a sharp recent rally.
writeup.thesis: DocuSign scores 69, a Buy, driven mainly by a perfect balance sheet score of 100 (net cash, no debt) and a strong trend score of 81, with the price 51.0% above its 200-day average and shares 70.1 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days. Quality scores 74 on a 79.5% gross margin and a 35.6% FCF margin, and the diluted share count is down 8.5% year on year, though stock-based compensation runs at 18.0% of revenue and the operating margin is 12.0%. Valuation scores 69: in absolute terms P/FCF of 12.8x is low for software, with an FCF yield 2.9 pp above the 10-year Treasury yield, while EV/EBIT of 36.2x is high. Against its own history it is cheap overall (EV/EBIT not comparable), with P/FCF cheaper than at 51 of the last 61 month-ends and P/S near the middle of the last 61 month-ends. Growth is the weak spot at 52, with TTM revenue growth of 8.6%, though growth sped up by 0.7 pp from the previous quarter.
key_risks: Revenue growth is modest, with TTM revenue growth of 8.6%, which caps the growth score at 52.
Stock-based compensation at 18.0% of revenue makes reported free cash flow look stronger than operating profit.
After a big run the price is 18.0% above its 50-day average and 3.8% below its 52-week high, so a pullback could hurt the trend score.
EV/EBIT of 36.2x is high in absolute terms, leaving little room if margins disappoint.
Analyst consensus is Hold, insiders made planned sales, and a disclosed PHP vulnerability investigation is a minor offset to product news.
what_would_change: A drop of 5 points would move the rating to Hold, for example from the trend score falling as the rally fades or growth slowing again.
Reaching Strong Buy needs 11 more points, most plausibly from faster revenue growth lifting the growth score of 52.
Progress on the raised FY2027 guidance, including IAM reaching about 18% to 19% of total ARR, could support growth and news scores.
Margin expansion or lower stock-based compensation would lift quality and bring EV/EBIT down.
